foodie.title: Pizza and the Back Bar at Young Joni
foodie.description: Ann Kim's wood-fired pizza with Korean inflections, plus a hidden back bar you enter from the alley if you know which door.
foodie.bonus: Find the back bar entrance off the alley rather than walking through the restaurant.

foodie.title: Sausage Counter at Kramarczuk's
foodie.description: A Ukrainian deli and sausage house in Northeast that has been curing, smoking and stuffing on the same corner since 1954.
foodie.bonus: Buy something from the deli case to take home, not just the lunch plate.

foodie.title: Arepas at Hola Arepa
foodie.description: A food truck that graduated into a bright Kingfield restaurant, still built on corn cakes stuffed with slow-cooked pork and plantain.
foodie.bonus: Get the plantains as a side even though you don't need them.

foodie.title: Handmade Pasta at Bar La Grassa
foodie.description: A North Loop room built around fresh pasta and small plates, famous for a soft egg and lobster bruschetta that has never left the menu.
foodie.bonus: Order two pastas for the table before anything else.

foodie.title: Dinner at Owamni
foodie.description: Sean Sherman's decolonized Indigenous kitchen above St. Anthony Falls — no dairy, wheat, cane sugar or pork, and a view straight down the river.
foodie.bonus: Ask which of the night's ingredients are Indigenous-sourced.

foodie.title: Settle the Jucy Lucy Argument at the 5-8 Club
foodie.description: The other claimant to the molten-cheese-inside-the-patty crown, directly across town from Matt's. Eat one here, form an opinion, defend it.
foodie.bonus: Wait the full minute before biting. People have been burned.

foodie.title: Fourteen Stools at Al's Breakfast
foodie.description: A ten-foot-wide Dinkytown diner with fourteen stools and no room to wait, where you stand behind a seated stranger until they leave.
foodie.bonus: Order the blueberry walnut pancakes and watch the grill from your stool.

foodie.title: Vietnamese Night at Hai Hai
foodie.description: Christina Nguyen's Northeast room serving Southeast Asian street food — bánh xèo, grilled skewers and tiki drinks under a lot of neon.
foodie.bonus: Order the bánh xèo and eat it wrapped in lettuce the way it's meant to be.

social.title: Beer Hall Night at Surly
social.description: The brewery that changed Minnesota's beer laws, in a cavernous destination hall with long communal tables and a yard out back.
social.bonus: Sit at a communal table with people you don't know.

social.title: Ferris Wheel and Bocce at Betty Danger's
social.description: A Northeast bar with a working Ferris wheel in the parking lot, a mini golf course, and an entirely committed sense of humour.
social.bonus: Take a drink up on the Ferris wheel.

social.title: Local Bill at the Turf Club
social.description: A 1940s St. Paul bar with a sunken Clown Lounge downstairs and a stage that has hosted Midwest bands on their way up for decades.
social.bonus: Go down to the Clown Lounge between sets.

social.title: Drag Night at the Gay 90's
social.description: A multi-level downtown institution running one of the longest-standing drag revues in the Midwest across several rooms and dance floors.
social.bonus: Get a seat for the revue rather than watching from the bar.

social.title: An Evening at Palmer's Bar
social.description: A West Bank dive that has been exactly itself since 1906 — cheap drinks, live music in the corner, and the best patio regulars in the city.
social.bonus: Talk to whoever has been sitting at the bar the longest.

social.title: Barcade Night at Up-Down
social.description: Quarter arcade cabinets, skee-ball, pinball and pizza by the slice on Lyndale, with a rooftop patio when the weather allows.
social.bonus: Run a full group tournament on one cabinet.

social.title: Rooftop at the Hewing Hotel
social.description: A North Loop rooftop with a heated pool deck and a sauna, which is a very Minneapolis way to handle a bar being outdoors in October.
social.bonus: Go when it's cold and use the outdoor fire.

social.title: Find the Door at Volstead's Emporium
social.description: An unmarked basement speakeasy off an alley in Whittier, low-lit and deliberately hard to find, with a cocktail list worth the hunt.
social.bonus: Don't look up the entrance. Find it.

culture.title: Improv Night at HUGE Theater
culture.description: A theatre devoted entirely to long-form improv, running several shows a night in a small room where nothing is scripted.
culture.bonus: Stay for the late show — it's looser and usually better.

culture.title: Wild Game at Xcel Energy Center
culture.description: The State of Hockey at full volume — eighteen thousand people who genuinely understand the game, in a building made specifically for it.
culture.bonus: Be in your seat for the anthem, not still in the concourse.

culture.title: Twins Game at Target Field
culture.description: An open-air downtown ballpark built from Minnesota limestone, with a giant animated Minnie and Paul sign that lights up for home runs.
culture.bonus: Get a seat where you can actually see the sign light up.

culture.title: Mill City Museum and the Ruin Courtyard
culture.description: A museum built inside the burned-out shell of what was once the largest flour mill on earth, with an observation deck over the falls.
culture.bonus: Ride the Flour Tower elevator show, then go up to the deck.

culture.title: Weisman Art Museum
culture.description: Frank Gehry's crumpled stainless-steel building on the riverbank above campus, free to enter, best seen in late afternoon light.
culture.bonus: Photograph the west facade from the Washington Avenue Bridge at sunset.

culture.title: Fika at the American Swedish Institute
culture.description: A 1908 Swedish-American mansion with hand-carved porcelain stoves, attached to a modern wing where you take coffee and cardamom buns.
culture.bonus: Find all the kakelugnar tile stoves in the mansion.

culture.title: The Minnesota State Fair
culture.description: The Great Minnesota Get-Together — twelve days, two million people, a butter sculpture of the dairy princess, and everything imaginable on a stick.
culture.bonus: Eat at least five things on a stick before you leave.

culture.title: Minneapolis Institute of Art
culture.description: An encyclopedic museum of ninety thousand works spanning five millennia, and the permanent collection is free every single day.
culture.bonus: Find the Chinese scholar's study reassembled inside the Asian galleries.

8ball.title: Pick a Lake and Walk All the Way Around It
8ball.description: There are more than twenty lakes inside the city. Choose one you have never circled on foot and walk the whole loop without cutting across.
8ball.bonus: Stop at the first place selling food that you pass.

8ball.title: Ride the Green Line to a Stop You've Never Used
8ball.description: Get on the Green Line between the two downtowns, pick a University Avenue stop you have never gotten off at, and eat at whatever is closest to the platform.
8ball.bonus: Take the first restaurant you see, not the best-reviewed one.

adventure.title: Float the Apple River
adventure.description: The Twin Cities summer ritual: an inner tube, a slow Wisconsin river, and four hours of drifting with a few hundred of your closest strangers.
adventure.bonus: Tie your group's tubes together before you put in.

adventure.title: Climb the Bluffs at Interstate State Park
adventure.description: Basalt cliffs above the St. Croix at Taylors Falls, full of glacial potholes and the closest real rock climbing to the Twin Cities.
adventure.bonus: Find the deepest glacial pothole on the Pothole Trail.

adventure.title: Ski the Groomed Trails at Theodore Wirth
adventure.description: The biggest park in the city keeps machine-groomed, snowmaking-backed cross-country trails, so it skis even in a thin winter.
adventure.bonus: Do a lap on the lit loop after dark.

adventure.title: Ride the Midtown Greenway End to End
adventure.description: A below-grade rail trench converted into a bike expressway that crosses the whole south side without a single traffic light.
adventure.bonus: Climb out at the Sabo Bridge and ride across it.

adventure.title: Paddle the Chain of Lakes Channels
adventure.description: Rent a canoe and thread the narrow tree-covered channels that connect Lake of the Isles, Cedar and Bde Maka Ska into one continuous paddle.
adventure.bonus: Do all three lakes without getting out of the boat.

adventure.title: Ice Fishing on Lake Minnetonka
adventure.description: Rent a heated house out on the ice, drill a hole, and spend a Minnesota afternoon doing very little with great commitment.
adventure.bonus: Stay out past dark for the evening bite.

adventure.title: Kayak the Mississippi River Gorge
adventure.description: Put in below the university and paddle the only true gorge on the entire Mississippi, with limestone bluffs on both banks inside the city limits.
adventure.bonus: Paddle up as far as the Franklin Avenue Bridge before you turn around.

adventure.title: Sunrise on the North Shore at Split Rock
adventure.description: Drive up before dawn and watch the sun come out of Lake Superior beneath the most photographed lighthouse in Minnesota.
adventure.bonus: Walk down to the pebble beach and shoot the lighthouse from below.

chill.title: Slow Morning at Spyhouse Coffee
chill.description: High ceilings, mismatched furniture and serious coffee — the Northeast and Whittier rooms are both good places to lose an hour.
chill.bonus: Sit at the window and don't open your laptop.

chill.title: Warm Up in the Como Conservatory
chill.description: A Victorian glass house in St. Paul kept at rainforest temperature all winter, free to enter, with a sunken fern room and a bonsai collection.
chill.bonus: Go in January, when the contrast with outside is the entire point.

chill.title: Eloise Butler Wildflower Garden
chill.description: The oldest public wildflower garden in the country, a fenced-off pocket of bog, prairie and woodland inside Theodore Wirth Park.
chill.bonus: Sit on the bench by the bog and wait for the birds to forget you're there.

chill.title: Browse Magers & Quinn
chill.description: The largest independent bookstore in the state, shelving used and new in the same aisles so you never quite know what you'll turn up.
chill.bonus: Leave with something from a section you never normally browse.

chill.title: Sunset From the Guthrie's Endless Bridge
chill.description: A cantilevered blue box that juts out of the theatre toward the river, open to the public whether or not you have a ticket.
chill.bonus: Find the yellow room window that frames St. Anthony Falls exactly.
